title: Linear combinations

review.history: source gap; no origin or priority assertions
review.interaction: implemented; numerical fixtures are not independent mathematical review

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. All stories and worked quantities are original constructed teaching scenarios, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate claim-level evidence before publication.
purpose: Build a new displacement from weighted copies of two vectors.
meaning: A linear combination scales vectors by real coefficients and adds them. Two independent plane directions span the whole plane when coefficients range over all real numbers; parallel or zero directions span less. The displayed coefficient box is only a finite part of that general construction.

definition.setting: Real vector spaces with an explicit two-dimensional coordinate model.

signature.ux,uy,vx,vy: Real vector components in [-3,3] on the same axes.
signature.r,s: Dimensionless real coefficients in [-2,2] in the UI; unrestricted real coefficients in the formal span.
signature.combinedX,combinedY: Components of the resulting vector w; combinedX is the primary numeric Graph output.
signature.determinant: u_x*v_y-u_y*v_x; nonzero means the pair spans the plane.

conditions: Vectors have the same coordinate dimension and compatible physical units; coefficients r and s are real, dimensionless scalars.
Scale both components of each vector, then add corresponding components.
The zero vector, zero coefficients and dependent vectors are valid inputs; no independence assumption is needed to form a linear combination.
The formal span uses all real coefficients. Bounded sliders display only part of that span.
definition.domain_notes: The formal definition extends to finite sums of vectors in any real vector space. The live model combines exactly two real plane vectors, each component in [-3,3], with coefficients in [-2,2]. This bounded coefficient region is not the entire span and is not a vector space. Negative coefficients reverse directions. Physical vector components must use compatible units; the shared model itself uses abstract coordinates. No target-solving or arbitrary number of vectors is implemented.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level reference; worked properties are author-derived for stated assumptions. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.formation_rule: output=combinedX=r*ux+s*vx; combinedY=r*uy+s*vy; firstX=r*ux; firstY=r*uy; secondX=s*vx; secondY=s*vy; norm=hypot(combinedX,combinedY); determinant=ux*vy-uy*vx.
grammar.precedence: Scale components before adding. Matrix products act on column vectors from right to left; an ordered pair retains its stated coordinate order.

grammar.ast_coverage: Both component sums and the full ordered vector appear in the AST. The primary scalar fixtures/Graph track combinedX, while scene and readouts retain combinedY. The span statement quantifies over all real coefficients; it is not a claim that a finite slider box is the whole span.

properties.claim: Zero coefficients always give the zero vector.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

properties.claim: If v=2u, every combination is (r+2s)u and the pair cannot span the whole plane.
properties.derivation: Factor r*u+s*(2*u)=(r+2*s)*u; all results stay in the one-dimensional span of u unless u is zero.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

examples.title: Combine two camera moves
examples.question: A camera rig has move u=(2,1) m and move v=(-1,2) m. What is one copy of each?
examples.setting: Original constructed teaching scenario; values and rules are stipulated, not measured.
assumptions: The vectors are displacements on one fixed coordinate grid; one grid unit represents one metre.
The two coefficients are dimensionless multipliers and may be negative or zero.
Displacements add ideally; obstacles, travel time and a routed path length are not modeled.

steps.reason: Scale both displacement components by their coefficients.

examples.interpretation: Two moves combine into one displacement arrow; its length is not the sum of their path lengths.

independent_check.expected: Starting at (2,1), translate by (-1,2) to arrive at (1,3); the straight endpoint distance squared is 1²+3²=10.

examples.limits: The path via the intermediate point has length 2sqrt(5) m, distinct from the net displacement length.

prompts.prompt: Must the weights add to one?
prompts.answer: No. That extra condition describes an affine combination; nonnegative weights adding to one describe a convex combination.

prompts.prompt: Do parallel vectors make the calculation undefined?
prompts.answer: No. The sum remains defined, but its full span is at most a line.
